Based on the search results, **Queen Camilla** is the spouse (wife) of the current British King, **King Charles III**.

Key details:
- **Marriage**: They wed on April 9, 2005, at Windsor Guildhall, followed by an Anglican blessing at St George's Chapel in Windsor Castle.
- **Becoming Queen**: When Queen Elizabeth II passed away on September 8, 2022, Charles ascended the throne as King Charles III, making Camilla the Queen Consort of the United Kingdom and other Commonwealth realms.
- **Coronation**: They were crowned together on May 6, 2023, at Westminster Abbey.
- **Previous Marriage**: Before marrying Prince Charles, Camilla was first married to Andrew Parker Bowles from 1973 to 1995 (they divorced).
- **Name**: Born Camilla Rosemary Shand, she is now known as Queen Camilla.

So if you're asking about "the British queen" in present tense, her spouse is King Charles III. If you're asking about the late Queen Elizabeth II, her spouse was King Philip (Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh), whom she married for over 73 years until his death in 2021.

**Camilla**(née**Camilla Rosemary Shand**, later **Parker Bowles**; born 17 July 1947) is Queen of the United Kingdom and 14 other Commonwealth realms as the wife of King Charles III.[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-realms-1)
Camilla was raised in East Sussex and South Kensington in England and educated in England, Switzerland and France. In 1973, she married British Army officer Andrew Parker Bowles; they divorced in 1995. Camilla and Charles were romantically involved periodically, both before and during each of their first marriages. Their relationship was highly publicised in the media and attracted worldwide scrutiny.

In 2005, Camilla married Charles in the Windsor Guildhall, which was followed by a televised Anglican blessing at [St George's Chapel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_George's_Chapel "St George's Chapel") in Windsor Castle. From their marriage until Charles's accession, she was known as the Duchess of Cornwall. On 8 September 2022, Charles became king upon the death of his mother, Queen Elizabeth II, with Camilla as queen consort. [Charles and Camilla's coronation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_and_Camilla's_coronation "Charles and Camilla's coronation") took place at Westminster Abbey on 6 May 2023.
Camilla carries out public engagements representing the monarch and is the patron of numerous charities and organisations. Since 1994, she has campaigned to raise awareness of osteoporosis, which has earned her several honours and awards. She has also campaigned to raise awareness of issues such as rape, sexual abuse, domestic violence, illiteracy, animal welfare and poverty.

## Early life and education
Camilla Rosemary Shand was born on 17 July 1947 at [King's College Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King's_College_Hospital "King's College Hospital"), London,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGraham20059-2)[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-3) the eldest of three children of Major Bruce Shand, a British Army officer turned businessman, and his wife Rosalind (née Cubitt), daughter of Roland Cubitt, 3rd Baron Ashcombe. She was baptised on 1 November at St. Peter's Church, Firle, East Sussex.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-4) Camilla has a younger sister, Annabel Elliot, and had a younger brother, Mark Shand.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-MarkShandDeath-5) The family divided their time between their 18th-century country house–The Laines[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-6) in Plumpton, East Sussex[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrandreth2007104-7)–and their London house in South Kensington.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrandreth2007107-8) One of her maternal great-grandmothers, Alice Keppel, was a mistress of King Edward VII.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-9)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-FOOTNOTESouhami19969-10)

## Early life and education
Rosalind was a charity worker[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-11) who during the 1960s and 1970s volunteered at the Chailey Heritage Foundation (which helps young children with disabilities) near their Sussex home. Bruce had various business interests after retiring from the army. He was most notably a partner in Block, Grey and Block, a firm of wine merchants in South Audley Street, Mayfair, later joining Ellis, Son and Vidler of Hastings and London.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-12)
During her childhood, Shand became an avid reader through the influence of her father, who read to her frequently.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-13) She grew up with dogs and cats,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrandreth2007105-14) and, at a young age, learnt how to ride by joining Pony Club camps, going on to win rosettes at community gymkhanas.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrandreth2007107-8)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-15) According to her, childhood "was perfect in every way".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrandreth2007104-7) Biographer Gyles Brandreth describes her background and childhood:

## Early life and education
> Camilla is often described as having had an "Enid Blyton sort of childhood". In fact, it was much grander than that. Camilla, as a little girl, may have had some personality traits of George, the tomboy girl among the _Famous Five_, but Enid Blyton's children were essentially middle-class children and the Shands, without question, belonged to the upper class. The Shands had position and they had help–help in the house, help in the garden, help with children. They were gentry. They opened their garden for the local Conservative Party Association summer fête. Enough said.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrandreth2007105-14)

## Duchess of Cornwall
### Foreign and domestic trips
In March 2012, the couple visited Norway, Sweden and Denmark to mark [Elizabeth II's Diamond Jubilee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_II's_Diamond_Jubilee "Elizabeth II's Diamond Jubilee").[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-152) In May 2012, they undertook a four-day trip to Canada as part of the jubilee celebrations.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-153) In November 2012, they visited Australia, New Zealand and Papua New Guinea for a two-week jubilee tour.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-154) During the Australian tour, they attended the 2012 Melbourne Cup, where Camilla presented the Melbourne cup to the winner of the race.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-155) In 2013, the couple went on a tour to Jordan, meeting with King Abdullah II and Queen Rania. They visited Syrian refugee camps of the civil war.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-156) Camilla attended the State Opening of Parliament for the first time in May 2013,[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-157) and the same month, she travelled to Paris on her first solo trip outside the United Kingdom.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-french-20) That same year, she and Charles attended the inauguration of Willem-Alexander, King of the Netherlands, as well as the preceding celebrations in honour of the departing Queen Beatrix.[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-158)[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-159)
In Rwanda, June 2022

## Duchess of Cornwall
### Foreign and domestic trips
In June 2014, Camilla and Charles attended the 70th anniversary commemorations of D-Day in Normandy, France,[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-160) and in November of that year, they embarked on a nine-day tour to Mexico and Colombia.[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-161) In May 2015, they visited Northern Ireland and undertook their first joint trip to the Republic of Ireland.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-162) In April 2018, they toured Australia and attended the opening of the 2018 Commonwealth Games.[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-163) They also toured the West African countries of The Gambia, Ghana and Nigeria in November 2018.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-164) In March 2019, Charles and Camilla went on an official tour to Cuba, making them the first British royalty to visit the country;

## Duchess of Cornwall
### Foreign and domestic trips
the tour was part of offers to strengthen UK–Cuban ties.[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-165) In January 2020, the Duchess, on behalf of the UK, attended commemorations in Poland to mark the 75th anniversary of the liberation of Auschwitz-Birkenau.[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-166) In March 2021, the couple went on their first official foreign visit since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic and visited Greece at the invitation of the Greek government to celebrate the bicentennial of Greek independence.[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-167) In March 2022, they visited the Republic of Ireland to commemorate [Elizabeth II's Platinum Jubilee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_II's_Platinum_Jubilee "Elizabeth II's Platinum Jubilee").[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-168) In May, the couple undertook a three-day trip to Canada as part of the jubilee celebrations.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-169) In June, Charles and Camilla made their first official visit to Rwanda to attend the 2022 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Kigali.[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-170)

## Queen consort
On her coronation day
Camilla became queen consort on 8 September 2022 upon her husband's accession as Charles III, following the death of Elizabeth II.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-Saunt-171) In his first address to the nation, Charles paid tribute to his "darling wife" Camilla for "the loving help and steadfast devotion to duty".[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-172)[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-173) On 10 September, she attended the Accession Council where Charles was formally proclaimed king and she served as a witness together with her stepson William.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-174)
Following the accession, Queen Camilla replaced the traditional role of lady-in-waiting with a new role of [queen's companion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen's_companion "Queen's companion"), which would be a more occasional and less formal role, assisting her at official engagements but not in replying to letters or day-to-day planning.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-175) She appointed the Marchioness of Lansdowne, the Baroness Chisholm of Owlpen, Jane von Westenholz, Lady Sarah Keswick, Lady Brooke, and Sarah Troughton to the role.[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-176)
On 13 February 2023, Camilla tested positive for COVID-19, which forced her to postpone a number of public engagements.[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-177)

## Queen consort
Camilla was crowned alongside Charles on 6 May 2023 at Westminster Abbey, London.[[176]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-178) On 16 June, the King appointed the Queen to the Order of the Thistle.[[177]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-179) On 5 July, she accompanied Charles to a national service of thanksgiving at [St Giles' Cathedral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Giles'_Cathedral "St Giles' Cathedral") where the Honours of Scotland were presented to him.[[178]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-180) Unlike the previous consort, Prince Philip, Queen Camilla would not receive a Parliamentary annuity and her activities would be funded through the Sovereign Grant instead.[[179]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-181)
In March 2023, the Queen accompanied the King for a state visit to Germany, which was his first foreign visit as monarch.[[180]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-182) In September and October, they undertook state visits to France and Kenya,[[181]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-183)[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-184) and in November, Camilla joined Charles at his first State Opening of Parliament as Sovereign.[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-185)
With Charles in front of the Sydney Harbour Bridge, 2024

## Queen consort
Due to the King's cancer diagnosis in 2024, the Queen deputised for him in his absence at the Commonwealth Day service at Westminster Abbey and at the Royal Maundy at Worcester Cathedral,[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-186)[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-187) making her the first consort to hand out the ceremonial coins at the latter event.[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-188) In June, they travelled to Normandy to attend the 80th anniversary commemorations of D-Day.[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-189) In October, the King and Queen toured Australia and Samoa.[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-190) In the following month she cancelled several of her public engagements due to a chest infection that was later revealed to be a form of pneumonia.[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-191)[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-192)

## Queen consort
Despite initially cancelling a planned Vatican visit, the King and Queen, while visiting Italy, made a surprise visit to the Vatican on 9 April 2025–their 20th wedding anniversary–to meet Pope Francis at Casa Santa Marta as he was recovering from pneumonia.[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-193)[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-194) Francis died 12 days later.[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-195) In May, she accompanied Charles on a two-day visit to Canada.[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-196) During the visit, she was sworn in as a member of the [King's Privy Council for Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King's_Privy_Council_for_Canada "King's Privy Council for Canada").[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-197) In July, the Queen was appointed Vice-Admiral of the United Kingdom, making her the first female to hold this title.[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-198) In September, she was forced to withdraw from attending the Duchess of Kent's funeral due to acute sinusitis.[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-199) In the following month, Camilla accompanied Charles on his state visit to the Holy See.[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-200)

## Queen consort
In March 2026, the Queen became the first female member of the royal family to join the Garrick Club.[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-201) In April, she accompanied Charles on a four-day state visit to the United States.[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-202) In September, the King and Queen, along with French president Emmanuel Macron, viewed the Bayeux Tapestry exhibition at the British Museum, marking the first time in over 900 years that the tapestry has returned to England from France.[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-203) In November, she accompanied Charles on a four-day visit to Antigua and Barbuda and attended the 2026 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting.[[202]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-204)

Title: Why King Charles and Queen Camilla spend their weekends apart after 20 years of marriage
Chunks: 0,1,2,3
**King Charles and Queen Camilla** have been married for more than 20 years, but their approach to married life might look a little unconventional from the outside.
You may also like
*      
*      
*
Continue reading
Despite their demanding schedules and shared royal responsibilities, the King and Queen reportedly make room for something that has long been part of their relationship, and that is their independence.
© -
King Charles and Queen Camilla have been married since April 2005 and have maintained a degree of independence in their private lives.
According to the Daily Mail’s royal editor Rebecca English, Charles and Camilla frequently spend portions of their weekends at separate country homes, with the King retreating to his beloved Highgrove House while Camilla enjoys time at Ray Mill House, the private Wiltshire property she has maintained since before marrying Charles.
“I can understand why it looks a little odd to people, but it actually works for them,” English said during a recent episode of the Daily Mail’s “Palace Confidential.”
© WPA Pool
King Charles visits the Highgrove stand at the RHS Chelsea Flower Show in May 2025. The monarch reportedly enjoys spending weekends at Highgrove House, where his passion for gardening has shaped the estate's celebrated gardens.

### Camilla was determined to keep her own home
Ray Mill House has remained an important part of Camilla’s private life for decades. Camilla purchased the property following the breakdown of her marriage to Andrew Parker Bowles, whom she divorced in 1995.
When she and Charles prepared to marry in 2005, questions reportedly arose over whether she would continue to maintain the residence, particularly because keeping a separate property required additional security.
© Keith Waldegrave/Mail On Sunday/Shutterstock
An aerial view of Ray Mill House, Queen Camilla’s longtime private retreat in Wiltshire, where she can enjoy a more informal life away from royal residences with her children and grandchildren.
According to English, Camilla “made very clear that she wanted to keep it.” The decision has allowed the Queen to retain a space removed from the formality that inevitably comes with royal residences.
“It’s a real bolthole for her. It’s very informal,” English explained. Camilla can spend time there with her children, Tom Parker Bowles and Laura Lopes, as well as her grandchildren, while Charles is able to pursue his own interests at Highgrove.
© David Jones - PA Images
Queen Camilla's private Ray Mill House in Wiltshire features an old mill pond surrounded by extensive gardens. The Queen has maintained the property since before her 2005 marriage to King Charles.
Charles does sometimes visit Ray Mill, according to English, but he often spends his weekends at Highgrove, where he famously has a deep interest in the gardens and grounds.
“They also live quite independent lives and I don’t think it affects their relationship at all,” English said.
© Getty Images
Queen Camilla complements King Charles with a striking red look at one of Britain's most important royal events.
The arrangement might also feel more natural to Charles and Camilla because independence was built into their relationship long before they became husband and wife. The pair spent years in one another's lives before eventually marrying, meaning they were already accustomed to maintaining separate homes and routines.

### A place where Camilla’s grandchildren can simply be themselves
Royal biographer Robert Hardman has also explained why maintaining Ray Mill House has particular importance for Camilla’s family.
© PA Images
Queen Camilla purchased Ray Mill House near Chippenham, Wiltshire, in the 1990s and chose to keep the private residence after marrying King Charles in 2005.
Unlike a royal palace, the private residence gives her children and grandchildren somewhere they can relax without worrying about royal protocol or the historic surroundings.
“Her grandchildren need to have somewhere that they feel is theirs, where they can run around,” Hardman said during the “Palace Confidential” discussion.
© David Jones - PA Images
A look inside one of the principal bedrooms at Ray Mill House, Queen Camilla's private Wiltshire retreat, which she purchased in the 1990s following the end of her marriage to Andrew Parker Bowles.
At their grandmother’s house, he explained, the atmosphere is considerably more relaxed. “When they’re at Granny’s house, it’s Granny’s house,” Hardman said. “Everyone can put on jeans and run around.”
For Camilla, the property therefore serves as more than simply a second residence. It offers a degree of normality for the family she had before becoming a senior member of the Royal Family and, eventually, Queen.

### Independence hasn't weakened their bond
Spending time apart certainly doesn't appear to mean Charles and Camilla are emotionally distant.
© Max Mumby/Indigo
King Charles and Queen Camilla reportedly spend some weekends apart, with the King at Highgrove House and the Queen at Ray Mill House.
Royal author Catherine Mayer explores their relationship in her 2026 book, “Divide & Rule,” describing the noticeable impact Camilla can have on the King when they are together.
“With Camilla, you only need to see her and Charles together to understand that she has this…magical effect on him,” Mayer wrote. “It’s transformative.”
© UK Press via Getty Images
Camilla reportedly insisted on keeping Ray Mill House after marrying Charles, preserving a private space away from royal residences.
Mayer recalled seeing Charles when he appeared tired or out of sorts, only for his demeanor to change once Camilla entered the room. “He would light up,” she wrote. “She just lifts him.”
The author also writes that, following the turmoil surrounding the end of Charles' marriage to Princess Diana and Diana's death in 1997, Camilla's place in his life became “non-negotiable.”
© Mark Cuthbert
Queen Camilla has maintained Ray Mill House, her private residence in Wiltshire, since before her marriage to King Charles.
Mayer argues that Charles understood Camilla was the person who could “really sustain him,” highlighting the emotional support she has provided throughout their decades-long relationship.

In 2005, Camilla married Charles in the Windsor Guildhall, which was followed by a televised Anglican blessing at [St George's Chapel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_George's_Chapel "St George's Chapel") in Windsor Castle. ## Early life and education
Camilla Rosemary Shand was born on 17 July 1947 at [King's College Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King's_College_Hospital "King's College Hospital"), London,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGraham20059-2)[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-3) the eldest of three children of Major Bruce Shand, a British Army officer turned businessman, and his wife Rosalind (née Cubitt), daughter of Roland Cubitt, 3rd Baron Ashcombe. She was baptised on 1 November at St. Peter's Church, Firle, East Sussex.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-4) Camilla has a younger sister, Annabel Elliot, and had a younger brother, Mark Shand.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-MarkShandDeath-5) The family divided their time between their 18th-century country house–The Laines[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-6) in Plumpton, East Sussex[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrandreth2007104-7)–and their London house in South Kensington.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBrandreth2007107-8) One of her maternal great-grandmothers, Alice Keppel, was a mistress of King Edward VII.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-9)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-FOOTNOTESouhami19969-10)

Rosalind was a charity worker[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-11) who during the 1960s and 1970s volunteered at the Chailey Heritage Foundation (which helps young children with disabilities) near their Sussex home. ## Queen consort
On her coronation day
Camilla became queen consort on 8 September 2022 upon her husband's accession as Charles III, following the death of Elizabeth II.[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-Saunt-171) In his first address to the nation, Charles paid tribute to his "darling wife" Camilla for "the loving help and steadfast devotion to duty".[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-172)[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-173) On 10 September, she attended the Accession Council where Charles was formally proclaimed king and she served as a witness together with her stepson William.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-174)
Following the accession, Queen Camilla replaced the traditional role of lady-in-waiting with a new role of [queen's companion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen's_companion "Queen's companion"), which would be a more occasional and less formal role, assisting her at official engagements but not in replying to letters or day-to-day planning.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-175) She appointed the Marchioness of Lansdowne, the Baroness Chisholm of Owlpen, Jane von Westenholz, Lady Sarah Keswick, Lady Brooke, and Sarah Troughton to the role.[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-176)
On 13 February 2023, Camilla tested positive for COVID-19, which forced her to postpone a number of public engagements.[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Camilla#cite_note-177)

Ray Mill House has remained an important part of Camilla’s private life for decades. Camilla purchased the property following the breakdown of her marriage to Andrew Parker Bowles, whom she divorced in 1995.

Despite their demanding schedules and shared royal responsibilities, the King and Queen reportedly make room for something that has long been part of their relationship, and that is their independence.

King Charles and Queen Camilla have been married since April 2005 and have maintained a degree of independence in their private lives.
According to the Daily Mail’s royal editor Rebecca English, Charles and Camilla frequently spend portions of their weekends at separate country homes, with the King retreating to his beloved Highgrove House while Camilla enjoys time at Ray Mill House, the private Wiltshire property she has maintained since before marrying Charles.
“I can understand why it looks a little odd to people, but it actually works for them,” English said during a recent episode of the Daily Mail’s “Palace Confidential.”
© WPA Pool
King Charles visits the Highgrove stand at the RHS Chelsea Flower Show in May 2025. The monarch reportedly enjoys spending weekends at Highgrove House, where his passion for gardening has shaped the estate's celebrated gardens.

### Camilla was determined to keep her own home
Ray Mill House has remained an important part of Camilla’s private life for decades. Camilla purchased the property following the breakdown of her marriage to Andrew Parker Bowles, whom she divorced in 1995.
When she and Charles prepared to marry in 2005, questions reportedly arose over whether she would continue to maintain the residence, particularly because keeping a separate property required additional security.
© Keith Waldegrave/Mail On Sunday/Shutterstock
An aerial view of Ray Mill House, Queen Camilla’s longtime private retreat in Wiltshire, where she can enjoy a more informal life away from royal residences with her children and grandchildren.
According to English, Camilla “made very clear that she wanted to keep it.” The decision has allowed the Queen to retain a space removed from the formality that inevitably comes with royal residences.
“It’s a real bolthole for her. It’s very informal,” English explained. Camilla can spend time there with her children, Tom Parker Bowles and Laura Lopes, as well as her grandchildren, while Charles is able to pursue his own interests at Highgrove.
© David Jones - PA Images
Queen Camilla's private Ray Mill House in Wiltshire features an old mill pond surrounded by extensive gardens. The Queen has maintained the property since before her 2005 marriage to King Charles.
Charles does sometimes visit Ray Mill, according to English, but he often spends his weekends at Highgrove, where he famously has a deep interest in the gardens and grounds.
“They also live quite independent lives and I don’t think it affects their relationship at all,” English said.
© Getty Images
Queen Camilla complements King Charles with a striking red look at one of Britain's most important royal events.
The arrangement might also feel more natural to Charles and Camilla because independence was built into their relationship long before they became husband and wife. The pair spent years in one another's lives before eventually marrying, meaning they were already accustomed to maintaining separate homes and routines.

### A place where Camilla’s grandchildren can simply be themselves
Royal biographer Robert Hardman has also explained why maintaining Ray Mill House has particular importance for Camilla’s family.
© PA Images
Queen Camilla purchased Ray Mill House near Chippenham, Wiltshire, in the 1990s and chose to keep the private residence after marrying King Charles in 2005.
Unlike a royal palace, the private residence gives her children and grandchildren somewhere they can relax without worrying about royal protocol or the historic surroundings.
“Her grandchildren need to have somewhere that they feel is theirs, where they can run around,” Hardman said during the “Palace Confidential” discussion.
© David Jones - PA Images
A look inside one of the principal bedrooms at Ray Mill House, Queen Camilla's private Wiltshire retreat, which she purchased in the 1990s following the end of her marriage to Andrew Parker Bowles.
At their grandmother’s house, he explained, the atmosphere is considerably more relaxed. “When they’re at Granny’s house, it’s Granny’s house,” Hardman said. “Everyone can put on jeans and run around.”
For Camilla, the property therefore serves as more than simply a second residence. It offers a degree of normality for the family she had before becoming a senior member of the Royal Family and, eventually, Queen.

Camilla reportedly insisted on keeping Ray Mill House after marrying Charles, preserving a private space away from royal residences.
Mayer recalled seeing Charles when he appeared tired or out of sorts, only for his demeanor to change once Camilla entered the room. “He would light up,” she wrote. “She just lifts him.”
The author also writes that, following the turmoil surrounding the end of Charles' marriage to Princess Diana and Diana's death in 1997, Camilla's place in his life became “non-negotiable.”
© Mark Cuthbert
Queen Camilla has maintained Ray Mill House, her private residence in Wiltshire, since before her marriage to King Charles.
Mayer argues that Charles understood Camilla was the person who could “really sustain him,” highlighting the emotional support she has provided throughout their decades-long relationship.
More than two decades after their 2005 wedding, their somewhat unconventional arrangement appears to reflect the relationship they have always had. Deeply connected, but comfortable giving each other space.

King Charles and Queen Camilla's relationship stretches back decades before their 2005 wedding at Windsor Guildhall.
For Charles, that might mean a weekend tending to the gardens at Highgrove. For Camilla, it can mean escaping royal formality at Ray Mill with her children and grandchildren.
It may be unusual for a King and Queen, but according to those who have followed their relationship closely, it works for them.
